elements.content: Communication Goal: I can describe another person's daily routine using the third person.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A0 General English
- Unit: Unit 4. Daily routine
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: A man of 100 faces
- Materials: Job cards, photo prompts, -s ending cards, COSYmanuals 'present simple' and 'question words' pages.
By the end of this lesson, you can:

• apply Present Simple 3rd person singular -s rules
• describe professional daily schedules

Quick retrieval task: which words or phrases do you remember?
Which word belongs to the previous lesson?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

eat — to put food in your mouth. Example: We eat lunch at one.
drink — to take liquid into your mouth. Example: I drink tea in the morning.
work — a job or activity you do. Example: I work in an office.
doctor — a person who helps sick people. Example: The doctor works in a hospital.
teacher — a person who helps students learn. Example: She is my English teacher.
man — a male person. Example: The man is a teacher.
tea — a hot drink made from leaves. Example: She drinks tea every day.
hard — with a lot of effort. Example: He works hard.
breakfast — the first meal of the day. Example: I have breakfast at eight.
every day — each day. Example: I study English every day.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• He works as a doctor. (talking about a job)
• He eats breakfast at six. (describing a routine)
• He drinks tea. (describing a habit)
• He works hard every day. (describing effort)
• She works in a hospital. (talking about a workplace)
• What does he do? (asking about a job)
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'to put food in your mouth'?
Which word means 'to take liquid into your mouth'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

eats /iːts/ — final /s/
drinks /drɪŋks/ — final /s/
teaches /ˈtiːtʃɪz/ — final /ɪz/

elements.content: Grammar Focus: Use the present simple for habits, routines, facts, and things that happen regularly.

Form:
Present simple: I / You / We / They + verb. He / She / It + verb + -s. Negative: don't / doesn't + verb. Question: Do / Does + subject + verb?

Examples:
• I work in a school.
• She works in a hospital.
• We don't work on Sunday.
• Does he drink coffee?
Controlled practice: choose the correct form.
He ___ tea every morning.
They ___ in a hospital.
She ___ like coffee.
___ you work here?
Substitution drill: say the sentence with the new words.

• I ... (work / study / live) in ...
• He ... (work / study / live) in ...
• They ... (don't / doesn't) ... on Sunday.
Question-answer practice: ask and answer with your partner.

• What do you do every day?
• Where does your best friend work or study?
• Do you drink coffee in the morning?
Personalised production: use the structure about your own life.

• Write three sentences about your daily routine.
• Write three sentences about a family member's routine.
Reading: A man of 100 faces

This is Mr Khan. He is a man of many faces. He works as a doctor in a big hospital. He eats breakfast at six and drinks tea. He works hard every day. He helps many people. His wife is a teacher. She works in a school. They are both busy, but they are happy.
What is Mr Khan's job?
What does his wife do?
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.

A: What does Mr Khan do?
B: He is a doctor. He works in a big hospital.
A: What time does he start work?
B: He starts at eight. He eats breakfast at six and drinks tea.
A: Does he work hard?
B: Yes, he does. He helps many people every day.
Where does Mr Khan work?
What does he drink?
Speaking task: Describe a family member's daily routine to your partner. Use 'he/she + verb-s'.

• What does your mother/father do?
• What time does he/she start work?
• Does he/she work hard?
• What does he/she do after work?
• Who is a busy person in your family?
Role-play: You are a journalist. Interview a classmate about a busy person they know and report the routine.
Work in pairs. Take turns. Use at least five target words and one target grammar structure. Then swap roles.
Writing task: Write five sentences about a family member's daily routine.
Model: He/She works ... He/She eats ... He/She drinks ... He/She goes ...
